difficulty_reason: Ordinary local-lemma bounds do not exploit repeated colors in connected violators enough to obtain the improved degree exponent. The authors erase at most2p vertices, encode a truncated tree walk and its repeated-color classes, and reconstruct every random color choice in forward and backward phases. A Catalan-counted execution trace and balanced color encoding contradict the entropy of failed runs, proving the bound. The complete original new core is explicit; supporting elementary estimates and helper statements are not separate units.
scope_text: Only the complete original Theorem 3, selected for positive integers \(p\) and finite graphs with maximum degree \(\Delta\ge1\): \(p\)-centered colorings use \(\mathcal{O}(p\Delta^{2-1/p})\) colors. The all-degree original statement remains intact; the edgeless case is not used to broaden the displayed formula. The complete Section 3 through its coloring-existence conclusion is selected, including Algorithm 1, truncated tree-walk erasure, both reconstruction phases and the Dyck/Catalan contradiction. The following expected-runtime discussion, planar/genus/topological-minor results and lower-bound variants remain unselected context, never additional units.
